questions.q: Fill up: SUI is defined as involuntary passage of urine on increase in ____ pressure.
questions.exp: The definition box prints 'Involuntary passage of urine on up in intra-abdominal pressure'.

questions.q: The printed examples of the precipitating acts in SUI are:
questions.exp: 'Eg. : Coughing, laughing, sneezing'.

questions.q: In the normal continence chain, raised abdominal pressure causes which muscle to contract?
questions.exp: The normal column prints pelvic floor muscle contracts.

questions.q: Which pressure rises in the normal chain to maintain continence?
questions.exp: 'Intraurethral pressure up' then maintains continence.

questions.q: The first event in the printed SUI chain is:
questions.exp: The SUI column starts with descent of bladder neck.

questions.q: Arrange the printed SUI chain in order - 1) Failure of urethra to close 2) Descent of bladder neck 3) Involuntary passage of urine 4) Rise in intra-abdominal pressure ... choose:
questions.exp: The column prints descent of bladder neck, rise in intra-abdominal pressure, failure of urethra to close, then involuntary passage.

questions.q: The diagrams on page 261 compare which two states with detrusor pressure arrows?
questions.exp: The two bladder sketches are labelled Normal and SUI.

questions.q: True/False: In SUI the urethra fails to close when intra-abdominal pressure rises.
opts: False - the urethra closes too early
questions.exp: The chain prints failure of urethra to close before leakage.

questions.q: Odd one out - which pressure change belongs to the normal continence chain rather than the SUI chain?
opts: Rise in intraurethral pressure maintaining continence
questions.exp: The intraurethral rise is printed only in the normal column.

questions.q: The test printed for SUI is:
questions.exp: 'Tests for SUI : Q tip test'.

questions.q: Fill up: The named test printed in the SUI box is the ____ test.
questions.exp: The tests box prints Q tip test.

questions.q: True/False: The methylene blue three swab test is printed under SUI rather than urinary fistula.
opts: False - it is printed under both
False - it is printed under OHSS
questions.exp: The three swab test appears in the urinary fistula tests box on page 262.

questions.q: The overall principle printed for SUI management is:
opts: Suspension of bladder neck or urethra
questions.exp: The management header prints suspension of bladder neck or urethra.

questions.q: Bursch colposuspension is performed by which route?
questions.exp: 'Abdominal route Sx' under Bursch colposuspension.

questions.q: In Bursch colposuspension which structures are suspended?
questions.exp: 'Proximal urethra & bladder neck suspended to'.

questions.q: The suspension in Bursch colposuspension is anchored to:
questions.exp: The line ends at iliopectineal/Cooper's ligament.

questions.q: The figure labels on page 261 for the Bursch procedure include which three structures?
opts: Obturator foramen, symphysis pubis and Cooper's ligament
White line of pelvic fascia, sacrum and Cooper's ligament
Retropubic space, symphysis pubis and obturator foramen
White line of pelvic fascia, symphysis pubis and iliopectineal ligament (Cooper's ligament)
questions.exp: The leader lines print those three labels with suture points a, b, c.

questions.q: Bursch colposuspension requires what regarding admission?
questions.exp: 'Hospital stay necessary' under the Bursch column.

questions.q: The outcome status printed for Bursch colposuspension is:
questions.exp: 'Good outcome : Gold standard'.

questions.q: Match each Bursch attribute with its printed value - 1) Route 2) Structures suspended 3) Anchor 4) Status ... A) Gold standard B) Abdominal C) Proximal urethra and bladder neck D) Iliopectineal/Cooper's ligament ... choose:
questions.exp: Abdominal route, proximal urethra with bladder neck, Cooper's ligament anchor and gold standard outcome.

questions.q: The two tension-free tapes printed are:
questions.exp: The tree prints tension-free transobturator tape (TOT) and tension-free transvaginal tape (TVT).

questions.q: TOT and TVT share which three printed attributes?
opts: Day care Sx, abdominal route and bladder neck suspended
Hospital stay, vaginal route and middle urethra suspended
Day care Sx, vaginal route and proximal urethra suspended
Day care Sx, vaginal route Sx and middle urethra suspended
questions.exp: The shared bracket prints day care Sx, vaginal route Sx and middle urethra is suspended.

questions.q: The tape in TOT is passed via:
questions.exp: 'Tape passed via obturator foramen' under TOT.

questions.q: The more common surgery between the two tapes printed is:
questions.exp: 'm/c Sx (TOT > TVT)'.

questions.q: The tape in TVT is passed via:
questions.exp: 'Tape passed via retropubic space' under TVT.

questions.q: TVT carries increased risk of injury to which structures?
questions.exp: 'up risk of injury to bladder & venous plexus' under TVT.

questions.q: The TOT/TVT figure on page 261 labels which pelvic spaces and foramen?
questions.exp: The leader lines print retropubic space and obturator foramen with TVT and TOT tapes.

questions.q: Match each tape with its printed route and risk - 1) TOT 2) TVT ... A) Retropubic space with bladder and venous plexus injury risk B) Obturator foramen and m/c Sx ... choose:
questions.exp: TOT goes through the obturator foramen and is m/c; TVT goes retropubic with bladder and plexus risk.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman with SUI wants a day-care vaginal procedure with the lowest bladder injury risk. The printed choice is:
questions.exp: TOT is the m/c day-care vaginal tape and the bladder injury risk is printed for TVT.

questions.q: Odd one out - which attribute belongs to Bursch colposuspension rather than the tapes?
questions.exp: The tapes are day care vaginal with middle urethra suspended; Bursch needs hospital stay.

questions.q: True/False: Both TOT and TVT suspend the middle urethra rather than the bladder neck.
opts: False - they suspend the bladder neck
False - TOT suspends bladder neck only
questions.exp: The shared bullet prints middle urethra is suspended.

questions.q: Constant dribbling of urine from the vagina with normal micturition indicates:
questions.exp: Complaint 1 prints that combination for ureterovaginal fistula.

questions.q: Constant dribbling of urine from the vagina with no normal micturition indicates:
questions.exp: Complaint 2 prints that combination for vesicovaginal fistula.

questions.q: Urine passed from both urethra and vagina during micturition indicates:
questions.exp: Complaint 3 prints urethrovaginal fistula.

questions.q: The types diagram numbers the three fistulae from above down as:
questions.exp: The sketch prints 1, 2, 3 with that legend.

questions.q: The types diagram labels which four pelvic structures?
questions.exp: The leader lines print ureter, uterus, bladder and vagina.

questions.q: Match each complaint with its fistula - 1) Dribbling with normal micturition 2) Dribbling with no normal micturition 3) Urine per urethra and vagina during micturition ... A) Urethrovaginal B) Ureterovaginal C) Vesicovaginal ... choose:
questions.exp: The complaint box pairs them in that order.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman after hysterectomy dribbles urine continuously yet passes normal volumes per urethra. The printed fistula is:
questions.exp: Preserved normal micturition with continuous dribbling is the ureterovaginal pattern.

questions.q: True/False: In vesicovaginal fistula the bladder empties wholly through the vagina, so normal micturition stops.
opts: False - only half the urine leaks
questions.exp: Complaint 2 prints no normal micturition with vesicovaginal fistula.

questions.q: The printed method of collecting a urine sample in fistula workup is:
questions.exp: 'Collection of urine sample : Suprapubic catheterization'.

questions.q: Menouria is defined on the page as:
opts: Urine passing per vagina during menstruation
Menstrual blood in urine sample only
questions.exp: 'Menouria : Hematuria during menstruation'.

questions.q: The two causes printed for menouria are:
opts: Endometriosis of bladder and ureterovaginal fistula
Endometriosis of bladder and vesicouterine fistula
questions.exp: The bullets print endometriosis of bladder and vesicouterine fistula.

questions.q: Fill up: Blood in urine appearing only during menstruation is printed as ____.
questions.exp: The box prints menouria with that definition.

questions.q: Odd one out - which cause is NOT printed for menouria?
questions.exp: Only endometriosis of bladder and vesicouterine fistula are printed.

questions.q: The methylene blue three swab test is the IOC for which fistula?
questions.exp: 'IOC for vesicovaginal fistula' under the test heading.

questions.q: How many swabs are placed in the vagina for the test?
questions.exp: '3 swabs placed at vagina'.

questions.q: The upper swab corresponds to which fistula?
questions.exp: 'a. Upper part : Corresponding to ureterovaginal fistula'.

questions.q: The middle swab corresponds to which fistula?
questions.exp: 'b. Middle part : Corresponding to vesicovaginal fistula'.

questions.q: The lower swab corresponds to which fistula?
questions.exp: 'c. Lower part : Corresponding to urethrovaginal fistula'.

questions.q: The dye is injected into bladder and urethra using which catheter?
questions.exp: 'Methylene blue dye injected into bladder & urethra by Foley's catheter'.

questions.q: An upper swab that is wet but unstained implies:
questions.exp: The table row prints upper swab wet, but unstained -> ureterovaginal fistula.

questions.q: A middle swab wet and stained blue implies:
questions.exp: The table row prints middle swab wet & stained blue -> vesicovaginal fistula.

questions.q: Only the lower swab wet and stained blue implies:
questions.exp: The table row prints only lower swab wet & stained blue -> urethrovaginal fistula.

questions.q: Why is the upper swab unstained in a ureterovaginal fistula?
opts: Because the swab is too dry
The dye enters below the ureteric leak, so ureteric urine bypasses the bladder dye
questions.exp: The dye is instilled into bladder and urethra; a ureteric leak above delivers unstained urine, matching the wet-but-unstained row.

questions.q: Match each swab position with its printed inference - 1) Upper wet unstained 2) Middle wet stained 3) Lower wet stained ... A) Urethrovaginal B) Ureterovaginal C) Vesicovaginal ... choose:
questions.exp: The table prints those three inferences in order.

questions.q: Scenario: After the three swab test the middle swab alone is wet and blue. The printed diagnosis is:
questions.exp: The middle swab wet and stained blue row is vesicovaginal fistula.

questions.unit: Vesicovaginal Fistula: Causes and Timing of Repair
questions.q: The most common cause of vesicovaginal fistula in developed countries is:
questions.exp: 'Developed countries : Total abdominal hysterectomy (TAH)'.

questions.unit: Vesicovaginal Fistula: Causes and Timing of Repair
questions.q: The most common cause in developing countries is:
questions.exp: 'Developing countries : Obstructed labour'.

questions.unit: Vesicovaginal Fistula: Causes and Timing of Repair

questions.exp: The immediate arm prints immediate repair.

questions.exp: The bracket joins identified after 24 hrs of Sx with post obstructed labour.

questions.q: The reason printed for waiting 6 weeks is:

questions.q: Match each identification timing with its printed repair plan - 1) Immediately after Sx 2) After 24 hrs of Sx 3) Post obstructed labour ... A) Repair after 6 weeks B) Immediate repair C) Repair after 6 weeks ... choose:

questions.unit: Vesicovaginal Fistula: Causes and Timing of Repair
questions.q: Scenario: A vesicovaginal fistula is recognised on day 5 after TAH. The printed plan is:

questions.exp: Identification beyond 24 hours routes to the 6-week arm.

questions.unit: Vesicovaginal Fistula: Causes and Timing of Repair
questions.q: True/False: Obstructed labour remains the commonest cause of vesicovaginal fistula in developing countries.

Young females, PCOS, obese female, raised follicle number, raised AMH, raised estradiol, multiple pregnancy and smoking
Older females, PCOS, thin female, raised follicle number, raised AMH, raised estradiol and pregnancy
Young females, PCOS, thin female, raised follicle number, raised antral count, raised AMH, raised estradiol and pelvic TB

Early OHSS is due to placental hCG

questions.q: hCG should be withheld if estrogen reaches:

questions.q: Cabergoline prevents OHSS by:
questions.exp: 'Cabergoline : down VEGF'.

questions.q: Embryo transfer is avoided in which situation?

questions.exp: 'No embryo transfer : If risk of OHSS +'.

questions.exp: The cloud prints estrogen 500 - 1500 pg.

questions.q: The ideal follicle number printed for hCG induction is:
questions.exp: 'Number : 2-3' in the follicles box.

questions.q: The ideal follicle size printed for hCG induction is:
questions.exp: 'Size : >17 mm'.

questions.q: The note at the foot of page 264 prints the amount of E2 released per follicle as:

questions.q: Match each prevention measure with its printed trigger - 1) Withhold hCG 2) Cabergoline 3) No embryo transfer ... A) Risk of OHSS positive B) Estrogen >= 2500 pg C) To lower VEGF ... choose:

Withhold hCG and avoid embryo transfer

questions.q: True/False: The ideal conditions cloud prints follicle size above 17 mm with number 2-3 for hCG induction.
questions.exp: The cloud prints number 2-3 and size >17 mm.

questions.q: Fill up: Cabergoline prevents OHSS by lowering ____.
questions.exp: 'Cabergoline : down VEGF'.
